title: Plan the electric car
target: Use circuit and mechanical evidence to plan a controlled motor-car test.
criteria: Predict effects of an open switch and a changed connection.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which sketch description makes a complete intended simple car circuit?
options: Battery positive → switch → motor → battery negative.
Battery positive → motor → unconnected wire.
Both motor terminals connected to the same battery terminal only.
Battery positive → wire → battery negative, bypassing the motor.
cpa.guide: The complete path includes both battery terminals and the load.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: What role should the switch play in a simple car circuit?
options: Replace the motor’s rotating shaft.
Open or close the motor’s intended current path.
Use up all current before it reaches the motor.
Create the battery’s chemical energy.
cpa.guide: A series switch controls circuit continuity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A car’s switch is closed but one return wire is loose and disconnected. Why will the simple model not run?
options: A closed switch guarantees current regardless of the other wires.
A return wire is never needed.
The motor must consume all battery charge at once.
The full circuit is open despite the closed switch.
cpa.guide: Every part of the intended series loop must connect.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: In an ideal simple permanent-magnet DC motor model, the supply polarity is reversed. What change is expected?
options: The current is converted into mass.
The motor torque and rotation direction reverse.
The battery voltage must become zero.
The switch disappears from the circuit.
cpa.guide: Reversing current relative to a fixed magnetic field reverses the turning effect.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A team wants to test wheel size. Which comparison best isolates that change?
options: Use predicted times as if measured.
Choose the single fastest run from unrelated cars.
Use the same car, battery condition, surface, and timing path; change wheel size and repeat trials.
Change motor, wheels, slope, and battery together.
cpa.guide: Keep other important conditions consistent and repeat to evaluate variation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Example runs over 3 m take 5.0, 5.2, and 4.8 s with one wheel set. What should be planned for a fair comparison with a second set?
options: Measure repeated times over the same 3 m under the same test conditions.
Select a result before testing.
Record just a guessed time.
Use a different downhill course for the second set.
cpa.guide: Consistent distance and conditions plus repeated measurements support the comparison.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
